mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units triggers a demand contraction that depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months indicates a contraction in manufacturing activity, which typically precedes earnings downgrades and negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent drop in CPI inflation below 2% signals a shift to an accommodative monetary regime, which typically supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL < 200 (i.e., < 2%) in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth above 400k per month for three consecutive months signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 400000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < 0% AND HOUST monthly change < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which typically boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 300).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL <= 300
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes with CPIAUCSL <= 300.
